protections.title: Itemized bill within 7 days
protections.plain: Ask the hospital for an itemized bill. A Florida hospital must send it within 7 days of your request.

protections.title: Answers about your bill in 7 business days
protections.plain: A Florida hospital must answer a question about your bill within 7 business days, and show the records behind the bill within 10 business days.

protections.title: Out-of-network specialists at an in-network hospital
protections.plain: At an in-network hospital, an out-of-network anesthesiologist, neonatologist, pathologist or radiologist can bill you only your in-network share. You cannot sign this protection away.

protections.title: Emergency care at in-network prices
protections.plain: For emergency care, an out-of-network hospital or doctor can bill you only your in-network share.

protections.title: At least 240 days to apply for financial assistance
protections.plain: A nonprofit hospital must accept your application for financial assistance for at least 240 days after the first bill after you left the hospital.

protections.title: Money back if you are approved
protections.plain: If you are approved for financial assistance, the hospital must refund what you already paid above your new amount, and undo collection actions.

protections.title: No more than insured patients pay
protections.plain: If you qualify for financial assistance, a nonprofit hospital cannot charge you more than it generally bills people who have insurance (AGB).

protections.title: No collections for 120 days, and written notice first
protections.plain: A nonprofit hospital cannot send you to collections, report you to credit bureaus or sue for at least 120 days after the first bill, and must warn you in writing at least 30 days before.

protections.title: Collections stop while your application is reviewed
protections.plain: Once you apply for financial assistance in time, the hospital and its collectors must pause collection actions until it decides.

protections.title: No denial for a document the form never asked for
protections.plain: The hospital cannot deny financial assistance because you did not send a document that its policy or form does not list.

protections.title: At least 180 days to appeal a denial
protections.plain: An employer health plan must give you at least 180 days after a denial to appeal it, and decide the appeal of a past service within 60 days.

protections.title: Without insurance: an estimate first, and a dispute if the bill is $400 over
protections.plain: Without insurance you can ask for a good faith estimate before care. If the bill is at least $400 more than the estimate, you can dispute it within 120 days of the bill.

protections.title: 3 years to sue over a hospital debt
protections.plain: In Florida, a lawsuit to collect a hospital debt must be filed within 3 years from when the hospital sent the debt to collections.

what_next_other_states: Outside Florida the federal protections above still apply. Rules on itemized bills, answers about a bill and collection lawsuits differ by state: look up your state's hospital billing law.
